principle: A domain operating system becomes more valuable when it can collaborate with other agentic systems through explicit agent cards, task contracts, memory boundaries, protocol choices, trust controls, streaming progress, traces, and recovery.

network_components.name: Agent Cards and Discovery
network_components.purpose: Define which agents or operating systems expose capabilities and how other agents discover, evaluate, version, and call them.
p0_blockers: agent capability exposed without owner or version
accepted tasks are not distinguished from refused tasks
remote agent discovery has no trust or verification path

network_components.name: Collaboration Topology
network_components.purpose: Map how internal agents, external agents, vertical operating systems, orchestrators, and event flows relate.
p0_blockers: multi-agent system has no ownership topology
delegation can recurse without anti-loop rules
separate operating systems share responsibilities without boundary

network_components.name: Delegation Boundaries
network_components.purpose: Define what one agent or operating system may ask another to do, what is forbidden, and what requires human approval.
p0_blockers: remote agent can perform public/paid/destructive work without approval
downstream agent receives broad context it does not need
delegated action has no audit attribution

network_components.name: Task and Message Contracts
network_components.purpose: Define structured request, response, refusal, timeout, idempotency, retry, and validation contracts for inter-agent tasks.
p0_blockers: inter-agent tasks rely on free-form prompts only
failure/refusal behavior is undefined
duplicate delegation can create duplicate external action

network_components.name: Protocol Surface Decision
network_components.purpose: Choose internal workflow, API/SDK, MCP, A2A-style agent protocol, event bus, browser automation, or Computer Use per boundary.
p0_blockers: MCP/tool access confused with agent delegation
A2A used for simple internal function calls
browser or Computer Use selected for production integration without accepted risk

network_components.name: Memory and Context Boundary
network_components.purpose: Control which memory, task payloads, artifacts, and user/domain context may cross agent or OS boundaries.
p0_blockers: raw private memory crosses domain boundary without approval
delete/export/correction does not propagate to shared artifacts
received context is trusted without prompt-injection handling

network_components.name: Identity, Auth, and Trust
network_components.purpose: Define caller/callee identity, scopes, token lifetime, tenant boundary, authorization event, and audit attribution for inter-agent calls.
p0_blockers: remote agent call cannot be attributed to user and agent
long-lived broad tokens cross systems
tenant boundary is unclear

network_components.name: Streaming and Progress Model
network_components.purpose: Define progressive updates, partial outputs, cancellation, stale job handling, and user-visible state for long-running remote agent work.
p0_blockers: long-running delegated work has no progress visibility
remote work cannot be cancelled
partial output can be mistaken for final output

network_components.name: Cross-Agent Observability
network_components.purpose: Trace discovery, delegation, context handoff, downstream tool calls, approvals, failures, retries, cost, and accountability across agents.
p0_blockers: bad delegated outcome cannot be reconstructed
downstream tool calls are invisible to the caller
cost/liability attribution is missing

network_components.name: Versioning and Compatibility
network_components.purpose: Manage evolving agent cards, task contracts, artifact formats, and external agent dependencies without breaking callers.
p0_blockers: caller depends on unversioned agent behavior
breaking changes have no migration path
external agent replacement strategy is missing

network_components.name: Reuse and Commercialization Opportunity
network_components.purpose: Identify which domain capabilities can become reusable internal services, agent cards, APIs, or marketplace surfaces.
p0_blockers: core reusable capability is duplicated across products without reason
public exposure is proposed without governance
marketplace ambition has no trust/version model

network_patterns.name: Social Content OS Network
network_patterns.first_interoperable_slice: domain OS sends approved insight package -> social content OS returns platform-ready draft package -> human approval -> publishing workflow remains governed

network_patterns.name: Market and Stock Intelligence OS Network
network_patterns.first_interoperable_slice: market intelligence OS produces approved thesis memo -> distribution or research specialist OS transforms it -> original OS records trace and approval outcome

network_patterns.name: Enterprise Operations Agent Network
network_patterns.first_interoperable_slice: frontline operations agent delegates a bounded specialist task -> specialist returns traceable decision package -> frontline agent asks for approval before external action

network_patterns.name: Creative Media Agent Network
network_patterns.first_interoperable_slice: content or campaign OS sends approved creative brief -> media specialist agent returns generated asset candidates and cost trace -> human selects approved asset

network_patterns.name: Multi-OS Ecosystem
network_patterns.first_interoperable_slice: one vertical OS exposes one agent card and consumes one external agent card through a typed, traced, approval-gated task contract
